Thanks for the details — quick update from platform side.

Summary: Coupa binds invites to the exact email address used when we create the supplier profile. If a customer's mailbox forwards to a distribution alias, Coupa may see the incoming acceptance attempt from the alias identity and treat it as an already-claimed account (NameID/email mismatch). Two safe options:

Option A (recommended, vendor-friendly): Resend the invite to purchasing@peakhardware.com (the alias). The procurement alias can claim the supplier and then we will open a merge/secondary-contact mapping to link Alicia's avargas@ address. This avoids the vendor needing to change mail rules. Potential caveat: if someone else previously claimed avargas@, we may need to merge manually.

Option B (lower-risk for identity duplication): Resend to a direct address that does not forward (e.g., avargas+redwood@peakhardware.com OR a secondary personal work address). Ask Alicia to accept from that direct mailbox; then we update the supplier contact list to add the purchasing alias.

Technical note: We can also send the raw claim URL (the direct token link) in the email body (Coupa link) instead of the normal invite template — it behaves the same but gives the vendor a one-click path. If you want that option, we can generate the link.

Action I'll take now: Ben, I'll regenerate the invite and include the raw claim URL and resend both to avargas@peakhardware.com and purchasing@peakhardware.com with a short note instructing purchasing to claim the tenant if they see the email. That should reduce friction.

Alicia — once you confirm receipt, accept from the address you prefer and let us know if the error repeats. If it does, send the screenshot and we'll proceed with a manual merge on our side.
